title: Learning to read from his uncle and starting on Dodds's E-flat clarinet
summary: His fiddle-playing uncle taught him to read music; Johnny Dodds lent him a small E-flat clarinet because his fingers were too small, and at 14 he bought his own B-flat clarinet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: How old were you when you started studying the clarinet?
Oh, I was about -- See, I studied music first. My uncle was a fiddle player, --
-- and he taught me music, how to read

music. Then when I got to read music good, then I got -- in the band I used to play in, the clarinetist was Johnny Dodds. He used to play parades and he used to use an E-flat clarinet, the small one because I was too small to have the B-flat. My fingers wouldn't reach the holes, you know. So he borrowed the E-flat from him so I could learn and I started on the E-flat. And then it wasn't so difficult for me to learn the notes and learn the fingering. You see, I knew the notes but I had to learn the fingering. So when I got started that way, then when I began to grow a little bit -- well, I was about eight years old, nine years old -- then my fingers, when they got a little larger, then I got the B-flat clarinet. I bought that myself. That was my own, and I was proud. And my godmother used to make me a little velvet sack. That was my case. When I was going to take my lesson, I'd put it in my hip pocket, you know, or put it under my arm and let my girl see it, you know.
She say, "Where you going?" "I'm going to take my lesson." "What you got there?" "My clarinet." Oh, boy, I was something else.
